articles.title: My local AI invented a receipt. It passed my math check.
articles.excerpt: I gave Qwen a receipt transcript with four text fragments and no digits. It came back with a purchase total of 12,000 rupiah, cash of 15,000, and 3,000 in change. The subtraction worked. The photograp…
articles.body: I gave Qwen a receipt transcript with four text fragments and no digits. It came back with a purchase total of 12,000 rupiah , cash of 15,000 , and 3,000 in change. The subtraction worked. The photograph said 230,000 . That's the row my first validation rule would have let into an expense sheet. I got to that row by following a question on Reddit. Someone with 16 GB of memory and a few hundred receipts to process wanted to know whether to give a small model the photos or run ordinary text recognition first. One reply suggested saving the photo pass for cases where the math broke. I liked that idea. I had access to a 16 GB Mac, and I wanted to know which receipts that rule would wave through. DEV authors have already built both kinds of importer.

articles.title: Like IDM, but free: I made a multi-connection download manager that also does torrents
articles.excerpt: []( url ) Like most of you, I grew up on IDM. It was fast, it grabbed everything from the browser, it just worked. Then the licenses got annoying, and torrent clients were a separate world entirely on…
articles.body: []( url ) Like most of you, I grew up on IDM. It was fast, it grabbed everything from the browser, it just worked. Then the licenses got annoying, and torrent clients were a separate world entirely one app for HTTP downloads, another for torrents, and nothing talked to your browser. So I thought why not make something like IDM, but with plexo multi-connection downloads (splits every file into chunks and pulls them through all your network adapters at the same time) and torrent support built in, with a browser extension that takes over downloads like IDM does. That became Qorvex. It's free and open-source, works on Windows, macOS and Linux. What it does: Multi-connection downloads — a file is split into chunks and downloaded in parallel, so you actually max out your bandwidth.

articles.title: Why I Built Lumina: A Local-First Markdown, AI Copilot, and Real Terminal Workspace in Tauri 2.0 + Rust
articles.excerpt: If you study, research, or write code every day, your desktop probably looks like mine used to: Obsidian or Notion open for Markdown notes and backlinks. VS Code or a terminal window open to run scrip…
articles.body: If you study, research, or write code every day, your desktop probably looks like mine used to: Obsidian or Notion open for Markdown notes and backlinks. VS Code or a terminal window open to run scripts, vim , or Git commands. Excalidraw open for spatial diagrams. A browser tab open to copy-paste context back and forth with an AI assistant . Alt-tabbing between four heavy apps breaks flow and running multiple Electron apps at once eats gigabytes of RAM just to edit plain text. So I built Lumina : a 100% local-first, open-source (MIT) desktop workspace powered by Tauri 2.0 + Rust and React 19 + CodeMirror 6 that brings Markdown notes, an infinite canvas, a vault-aware AI copilot, and a real pseudoterminal into a single fast app.

articles.title: From AI Agents to Type-Safe APIs: The Developer Productivity Playbook for 2025
articles.excerpt: Originally published on tamiz.pro. Developer productivity is no longer about adding autocomplete to an editor. Modern teams are stitching together AI agents that plan and execute work, type-safe contr…
articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . Developer productivity is no longer about adding autocomplete to an editor. Modern teams are stitching together AI agents that plan and execute work, type-safe contracts that keep services and clients in sync, and automated feedback loops that turn every change into a verifiable event. The result is not a single magic tool but a compounding system: agents move faster because they operate on precise context, type-safe APIs remove an entire class of integration bugs, and CI becomes the execution environment for both humans and machines. This playbook shows how to build that system incrementally. It covers the architecture, the contract-first workflow, agent permissions, evaluation gates, and the metrics that tell you whether the investment is paying off.

articles.title: Resume keywords for ATS: how matching really works
articles.excerpt: Originally published at https://cv0.org/en/blog/resume-keywords-ats There is no universal keyword list that makes a CV qualified. The useful keywords are in the posting in front of you, and the only o…
articles.body: Originally published at https://cv0.org/en/blog/resume-keywords-ats There is no universal keyword list that makes a CV qualified. The useful keywords are in the posting in front of you, and the only ones worth adding are the ones your work already supports. An applicant tracking system, or ATS, helps an employer manage applications. When discussing keywords, separate three questions: can the system extract your information, can a search find it, and does the information show you can do the job? Parsing extracts information. A parser may turn the document into profile fields such as your name, employers and employment dates. Greenhouse describes this process in its resume parsing documentation . It also explains that some formatting can cause incomplete extraction.

articles.title: I built a daily guessing game from museum open-access data
articles.excerpt: Doohickey is a free daily web game. Every day you get three real museum objects with the label covered, and you guess what each one was used for. 👉 https://playdoohickey.com You see a photo and what…
articles.body: Doohickey is a free daily web game. Every day you get three real museum objects with the label covered, and you guess what each one was used for. 👉 https://playdoohickey.com How it plays You see a photo and what the museum record says: what it's made of, how big it is, and where and when it was made. There are four options. Pick the one you think is right. The twist is hedging. If you're torn, you can pick two or three: one pick, and it's right: 6 points two picks with the answer among them: 4 points three picks with the answer among them: 3 points So two picks beat one whenever your second guess looks more than half as likely as your first, and "one or two?" becomes a real decision. A perfect day is 18.

articles.excerpt: Three stars, 28 light-years, and one big cosmic mystery.
articles.body: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour.

articles.title: Ariane 6 launch of 36 Amazon Leo satellites postponed due to a technical issue
articles.excerpt: The next launch attempt will be no earlier than Nov. 24.
articles.body: Amazon's first satellite launch since a rocket failure doomed 40 of its spacecraft has been postponed due to a technical issue. An Ariane 6 rocket carrying 36 satellites for the Amazon Leo constellation was scheduled to lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou, French Guiana, on Monday (Nov. 23). However, the countdown was halted following a technical issue affecting the rocket's ground support systems, according to Arianespace . The countdown was stopped before the removal of the mobile gantry, with Arianespace confirming that the rocket and its satellite payload remain safe and stable. Technical teams are now assessing the issue, with the next launch opportunity no earlier than Tuesday (Nov. 24).
